title: B — Private garden suites and dressing buffer
summary: Proposed 2D layout, unbuilt and not native-verified. Both sleeping rooms sit behind street-facing dressing/bath buffers; wider wings support mixed dressing and a working pantry.

area.convention: Floor-planning grid including wall allowances; open courtyard excluded. Not a cladding-face or site-area survey.

tradeoffs: Both king rooms move behind the street-facing dressing/bath buffers for privacy; they lose direct front-gable bedroom glazing.
The courtyard is narrower and longer (16 × 32 ft); side-room planning width grows to 19 ft, but the rear public band is about 15 ft 5 in deep.
Each compact 39 × 66-in clear proposed WC uses a 30-in pocket opening; product and local review are required.
The pantry has a 24 × 54-in prep/storage island, 42-in proposed west work aisle and 36-in east shelf-access aisle. It is useful but deliberately modest.

A dedicated 4 × 6-ft mechanical room occupies 24 sq ft of the living corner; removable panels face a 4-ft gallery service approach. Acoustic, installation and replacement requirements remain unselected.

status: layout proposal only; no Blender, IFC, render or geometric verification produced
notes: This is a furnished 2D proposal, not native-measured or approved construction geometry.
Room bounds are gross planning zones. Office/guest excludes the overlapping hall-bath rectangle; living excludes the 24-sq-ft mechanical room. These are not added to the 2,800-sq-ft total.
Front gable daylight serves dressing/bathing buffers rather than king rooms; reconcile the exterior glazing and ceiling sections if this option is selected.
Mixed dressing uses 24-in hanging, an 18-in drawer tower and approximately 13-in shoe/shelf depth. The proposed 12-in drawer travel needs a suitable real asset and a person-use check.
Laundry stain sink and pantry prep sink face opposite sides of the shared wet wall. Plumbing, wall build-up and access are concept reservations, not engineered routes.
Side bedroom windows flank deliberate solid headboard bays. Office glazing starts above its headboard.
Hall bath uses a 33-in pocket with northward travel ending at y = 34, leaving 6 in before the office opening; office and suite bath entries swing into their rooms without a basin conflict.
Laundry supply storage is on the south wall; no cupboard blocks the west entry or machine standing zone.

The 4 × 6-ft mechanical room includes separate 2.5 × 2.75-ft air-handler and 2.2 × 2.2-ft hot-water allowances. Its 5.5-ft removable panels face a 4-ft gallery service/removal approach. Exact plant, air requirements, acoustics and manufacturer service conditions remain unselected.
Both bathrooms use wall-backed fitted tubs, sealed surrounds and wall-mounted fillers. Maintenance access faces the dry aisle; no inaccessible rear cleaning sliver is proposed.
Street bath, WC and dressing windows use high obscured daylight glazing with opaque internal night shades. Obscured glass alone does not guarantee protection against silhouettes.
Both compact WCs use premium integrated-bidet/TOTO-style intent, with no exact product or approved power, water or service specification.

Both ensuite WC pockets retract toward the street, entirely within their enclosure-side wall. The wall no longer extends into the vanity standing zone; cavity endpoints are y = 0.375–2.875 ft for the proposed 30-in leaf.

Kitchen refrigeration is a proposed 48-in pair of true cabinet-depth integrated columns, 25-in enclosure depth, with panel fronts flush at x = 59.6667 ft with adjacent joinery. A 10.5-in south return-wall filler and 9-in north filler reserve hinge/handle relief. The matching full-depth overhead enclosure shares the same front plane. Exact hinge opening angle, drawer/bin removal, ventilation and service must be checked for selected products; the older 31.8-in-deep native asset is not adopted or claimed to fit.

Two compact laundry stacks each reserve24-in width and33-in depth including connection allowance: four machines total. Their smaller drum capacity is an explicit Option B tradeoff. Both full machine fronts receive a48-in-deep proposed operating zone without sink-base intrusion. The3-ft entry pocket retracts south into y27..30; freestanding utility storage fixes only to the south solid wall, with no pocket-cavity fasteners or services. Machine/sink use is sequential because occupied zones overlap. Products, stacking kits, upper reach and actual door/maintenance geometry remain to check.

The pantry island is an open-shelf worktable with no projecting drawers. Shared-wall shallow drawer travel is limited to18in, leaving24in occupied standing allowance in the42-in aisle; no27-in-travel native drawer asset is assumed.

Each dressing room has a3-ft cased opening from its private bedroom rather than a swinging leaf beside the king bed. Bathroom doors remain separately closable. Dressing street glazing retains its opaque night shade.
